sections.content: How many people are "quality assurance and regulatory professionals"?

91,005 people

were counted on the census as "quality assurance and regulatory professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Quality assurance and regulatory professionals organise and co-ordinate the effective measurement, monitoring and reporting on the qualitative and regulatory aspects of a specified tangible (industrial production) or non-tangible (service provision) output.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "quality assurance and regulatory professionals", 14.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "quality assurance and regulatory professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

  • special and additional needs education teaching professionals
  • managers in logistics
  • construction project managers and related professionals

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "quality assurance and regulatory professionals" there were a similar number of men and women (50.6% compared with 49.4%).

This means "quality assurance and regulatory professionals" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 50.6% and women made up 49.4% of "quality assurance and regulatory professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "quality assurance and regulatory professionals" included:

  • advertising accounts managers and creative directors
  • police community support officers
  • chartered and certified accountants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "quality assurance and regulatory professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "quality assurance and regulatory professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "quality assurance and regulatory professionals", 8.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (90% compared with 10%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.3%) than self-employed (2.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
